transcript.text: w/m finally died after 12 yrs, whats the best one to buy under £400? family of 5

For a family of five and a £400 ceiling, I’d prioritise a 9 kg machine (10 kg if you regularly wash bedding), 1400 rpm spin, a quick 30–60 minute wash, and a proper parts/labour warranty. At this price, a straightforward 9 kg model from a well-supported mainstream brand is usually a better bet than paying extra for Wi-Fi, steam or lots of programmes; buy from a retailer with delivery, fitting and old-machine removal included if possible. Check the machine depth as well as width—many 9–10 kg models project further than expected under a worktop. Before spending £400, it is worth ruling out a simple power problem on the old one: check whether it has any lights or display at all, and whether another appliance works from the same socket. If it is completely dead, the socket, plug fuse or internal power/control side are possibilities; if it powers up but will not run, it may still be an economical repair depending on the symptom.
it does power on, lights flashing. stopped mid-cycle 2 days ago with water still in the drum, wont drain or spin, just hums. would repair if its cheap

This sounds much more like a drainage fault than a dead washing machine: it will normally refuse to spin while water remains in the drum. The humming makes a blocked filter, something caught in the pump, or a blocked drain hose more likely than a motor problem; a failed pump is still possible if those are clear. With it switched off and unplugged, put towels and a shallow tray down, then open the small lower-front flap/kick-plate if fitted. Drain any water slowly via the little emergency hose if there is one, or loosen the filter gradually. Remove the filter and clear coins, hairpins, fabric etc.; then use a torch and gently check that the small impeller behind it is not jammed or damaged. Don’t force the door open with water still inside. If the filter and impeller are clear, inspect the drain hose at the back for a kink or squash. A blockage is often a free repair; if it is clear but it still only hums and will not pump out, the drain pump is the likely inexpensive repair for an engineer.
didn't know there was a filter tbh. where is it exactly? bottom front? water's still in the drum so what's the safest way to do it

Yes—usually it is at the bottom front, often behind a small square/rectangular flap on one side. On some machines there is no flap: the whole narrow kick-strip along the bottom front unclips or is held by a couple of screws, so do not force it if it does not obviously release. With water in the drum, switch it off at the socket and unplug it first. Put plenty of old towels down, plus a shallow tray, roasting tin or baking tray. If you find a little emergency drain hose, pull it out, remove its bung and empty it into the tray a bit at a time. If there is only a round filter cap, turn it anti-clockwise very slowly—just enough for water to trickle out—then pause, empty the tray and repeat. Expect several litres, so go slowly. Once the water has stopped, fully remove the filter, clear any debris, and check the small impeller behind it gently with a torch; it should not be solidly jammed. Refit the filter straight and firmly afterwards, or it can leak. A blocked filter/pump area remains the most likely cheap fix; if it is clear, the drain hose or pump itself becomes more likely.
ok will try that. hotpoint WMBF944P if that helps. anything else i should know before i open it?

Yes. The main thing is to expect more water than seems possible, so keep the tray low and empty it repeatedly rather than undoing the filter quickly. On this Hotpoint, look for a lower-front access flap or removable plinth; if a panel does not come away easily, do not lever or force it. Keep the machine unplugged throughout, and avoid tipping it while it is full of water. Before refitting the filter, wipe the filter seal and its seating clean, then screw it back in straight and snug—not cross-threaded—as a poorly seated filter can cause a leak on the next drain. Have gloves handy as coins, pins or broken plastic can be in there. The humming with retained water still points first to a blockage around the filter/impeller, then a hose restriction, with the drain pump itself also possible if everything is clear. Once the water is drained, what do you find in the filter and at the small impeller behind it: debris, a jam, damage, or does it turn with slight resistance?
ok, haven't opened it yet, will do it now. back in a bit with what i find

No rush. Keep the machine unplugged, drain the water slowly into a shallow tray with towels ready, and do not force any panel or the filter cap. Once you can see inside, note whether there is debris in the filter and whether the small impeller behind it turns with a little magnetic resistance rather than being solidly stuck. That result will tell us whether this is likely to be a free clear-out or a small pump repair.
